_source: myInstances -> MyInstancesResponse { success, message, error, metadata, data: [MyInstance!] }. MyInstance introspected live: appKey:String!, creditBurnUsd:Float, detailId:ID, id:ID!, instanceId:ID, name:String, plan:String, ram:String, renewsAt:DateTime, status:String!, vcpu:Int. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE PLAN RECORD, both checked against the handler: (1) ram and vcpu are NO LONGER hardcoded null - my-instances.handler.ts reads renderRam(instance.ramMb) and instance.vcpu for every instance-backed row, so the plan record's 'hardcoded null' line is stale; what IS still hardcoded null is creditBurnUsd, because the credit ledger has not landed. (2) appKey makes an app's TEMPLATE identity a first-class published field - a provisionable_apps key, deliberately a String and not an enum - so the kind badge is a real two-query client-side join on appKey === catalogItems[].templateKey rather than an assertion of shape. detailId is the expert_sites / agent_workspaces row id, which is what joins a row here to a row in my-expert-sites.fixture.json. THE ORPHAN ROW IS DELIBERATE: it proves the null arm, and note that the orphan pass publishes the TIER NAME in `plan` where the spine publishes the plan CODE. No count, no total: the query takes zero arguments.
